En önemli kısmı ise online eğitim sürecinde Refet Hocanın tutumuydu. Refet Hoca bütün derslere 20 dakika geç gelerek her seferinde sınıftaki 70 kişiyi bekletti. Tabiki hocamızın programının yoğun olduğunu tahmin edebiliyorum ama her geç geldiğinde bilerek aldırışsız davranması hiç hoş değildi. Refet hoca, öğrencilerine dünya ve Türkiye üzerine nasıl bir makroekonomik bakış açısının oluşturabileceğini bu dersi 20 yıldan uzun süredir vererek ispat etmiş, Bilkent İktisat'ın adeta parlayan incisi olmuştur. Öğrencilerine ilk haftalarda makroekonominin ölçüm araçlarından bahsederek minik ekonomistlere veri bulma toplama işlerini öğretmiş, ilerleyen haftalarda ise ülkenin yegane problemleri olan ekonomik başlıkları tamamıyla anlatarak öğrencilerine yaşadıkları dünya ve ülke hakkında aktif fikir oluşturabilmelerine elinden geldiğince yardım etmiştir. Derslerinde gerektiği noktada matematiksel analizin de dibine vurarak modellerin matematiğini anlamamıza yardımcı olmuş, gerektiğinde de gerçek hayattan bizlere ulaştırdığı, bazen de kendisinin anıları olan ülke ve dünya ekonomik olaylarını o anki anlattığı konuya da yardımcı materyal olacak şekilde ulaştırmıştır. Derse geldiğinizde ve dersten çıktığınızda eğer onun istediği gibi dinleyip notunuzu tuttuysanız anlattığı konuyu öğrenmiş ve o konu hakkında analiz yapabilecek, içerik tüketebilecek bir birey haline dönüşmüş olursunuz. Refet hoca, benim için öğretme eylemini başarmak konusunda eğitim bilimlerinin sınırlarını zorlayabilecek biçimde güçlü bir şekilde işini başarabilen biridir, ve anlattığına her zaman heyecanı olduğu için size de hiçbir fikriniz olmayan bir konu hakkında bir merak uyandırarak işler dersi. The strongest point of the instructor is that his way of teaching the course is able to bring the attention of the students and understand the concepts, as well as relate them to real life. However, the weakest point of the instructor is that while he is a very good teacher, who shows their interest in the subject they teach and how knowledgable they are, as a teacher of an introduction level of a subject, I do not think that his expectations on the students and the level of knowledge he thinks they possess is what it should be. While a course being introduction level does not mean that teachers should begin from the level taught in high schools or lower levels, at the very least, it should assume that since not everyone in the class is on the same level in terms of education regarding the topic, more background information should be provided before the actual content that is trying to be taught (and requires understanding of other topics). Even if this is not provided, with reasons such as the teacher not being there to actually guide the students to the answers each time or this being the student's responsibility, even the act of actually telling what concepts one should be familiar with that is not a part of the curriculum to understand the topics discussed in class before/during/after the lessons would have helped both the students and the teacher, who could have been frustrated during class when a student wasn't able to answer their question.
Another weak point was that while asking a question to students is a very good way to make sure they keep up with the lesson and test their understanding, I feel like it has caused some students to pay less attention due to anxiety or even led to them not  coming to lessons. While these consequences are primarily on the students and have no effect on the instructor, and it is important for them to get over these issues, if it affects their learning and doesn't even work, it can lead to the lesson being ineffective.

Although Refet hoca’s teaching style may need a bit getting used to and he can act a bit rude at times it’s clear that he is very knowledgable in his field and enjoys teaching. The best thing I can say is that, you might not like him, but you *will* learn from him.

There are several strong aspects to the course, but if I had to state one, it would be that we were motivated to learn what there was to learn about macro at this level and apply it to real life, like how the economy of our country is performing. The homework assignments were great in this respect. They were enjoyable to work on and very informative, also pushing us to think critically and acquire new skills. 

A weak aspect of the course is the grading system in exams. This overrides any and all strong aspects of the course. It is not student-friendly... at all... I understand the instructor's frustration with terribly wrong answers, however, a 0 is fitting enough of a punishment. 
I believe negative points are EXTREMELY counterproductive. When a student gives an answer to a question (whether they put effort and thought into it or not) they still spend some time in their limited examination period to write an answer. If they are wrong, they are already awarded nothing for their effort. A negative point actually takes away correct answers too, so it is as if they never answered either question. This is absolutely unfair. Furthermore, it demotivates students to answer because someone receiving some negative points for a question gets a lower point than someone who might have left that question blank. So there is no motivation to answer a question when it is so easily considered "out of range" or "out of context". It is important that the student learns what they do not know. I believe the giant "0" in red, in the middle of the paper is a good enough indication of what they do not know. 

Furthermore, no student has laid eyes on the answer key of the midterm exam. The TA's were not given the answer key during the period where we see the papers, no one knew acceptable answers even when they received negative points. So not only does the grading system of this course punish (rather than not awarding), it also fails to provide clarifications. Out of characters :)
